paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: trials aren't the end of you, they're the oven. James says to consider it "pure joy" when you run into trials of many kinds, because "the testing of your faith develops perseverance" (James 1:2-3). I'm not saying the heat feels GOOD. I'm saying a batch needs it, and so do you, so that you may be "mature and complete, not lacking anything" (James 1:4).

And when you're in the heat and you don't know what to do? Ask. James says if any of you lacks wisdom, ask God, "who gives generously to all without finding fault" (James 1:5). He asks us to come in faith, not tossed around like "a wave of the sea" (James 1:6). When trouble hits, you don't have to figure it out alone, because the One who gives wisdom is standing right there with His hands open.

Now here's the part to hold onto. A trial is not God tempting you, because "God cannot be tempted by evil, nor does He tempt anyone" (James 1:13). The pull toward sin comes from our own desires (James 1:14-15), but "Every good and perfect gift is from above," from a Father with "no change or shifting shadow" (James 1:17). He chose us "through the word of truth" (James 1:18), and those who persevere will receive "the crown of life" that He has promised to those who love Him (James 1:12). So stand firm, friend, and keep asking, because the One who gives never changes.
